body.statement: On the bounded observed-record domain \(\mathcal O\), consistency, armwise conditional exchangeability, and overlap imply \(\mu_a(x)=\mathbb E_P[Y_a\mid X=x]\) for \(a\in\{0,1\}\) and \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\). Hence \(\tau(x)=\mathbb E_P[Y_1-Y_0\mid X=x]\), \(m=\mu_0+\pi\tau\), \(\lvert Y_a\rvert\le1\) almost surely, \(\lvert\mu_a\rvert\le1\), \(\lvert m\rvert\le1\), and \(\lvert\tau\rvert\le2\). Operationally, the released observed-data factors obey \(\lvert B_l(X)A Y\rvert\le K_B\), \(\lVert F_{lj}(O)\rVert_2\le K_BK_\Phi\), and \(\lVert M_j(O)\rVert_2\le K_\Phi\).
body.justification: This separates the operational privacy support restriction on observed records from its causal identification and bounded-kernel consequences.
body.gap: Schröder, Melnychuk, and Feuerriegel assume a bounded observed outcome domain for private CATE learning; the present lemma records exactly how that observed-data restriction propagates through the causal model and this query.
body.consumer: It licenses the complete sensitivity ledger without assuming bounded unobserved potential outcomes as a primitive condition.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(a\in\{0,1\}\).  By consistency, on \(\{A=a\}\) one has \(Y=Y_a\).  By armwise conditional exchangeability, for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\) and every Borel set \(E\),
\[
 P(Y_a\in E\mid A=a,X=x)=P(Y_a\in E\mid X=x).
\]
Overlap makes the conditioning event non-null because \(P(A=a\mid X=x)\ge e_0\).  Therefore
\[
 \mu_a(x)=\mathbb E[Y\mid A=a,X=x]
 =\mathbb E[Y_a\mid A=a,X=x]
 =\mathbb E[Y_a\mid X=x]
\]
for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\).  Applying the same argument to \(E=\mathbb R\setminus[-1,1]\), and using that the observed record belongs to \(\mathcal O\), gives
\[
 P(|Y_a|>1\mid X=x)=P(|Y|>1\mid A=a,X=x)=0.
\]
Integrating over \(P_X\) proves \(|Y_a|\le1\) almost surely.  Conditional Jensen then gives \(|\mu_a(x)|\le1\), while iterated expectation gives
\[
 m(x)=\pi(x)\mu_1(x)+(1-\pi(x))\mu_0(x)
 =\mu_0(x)+\pi(x)\tau(x).
\]
Thus \(|m(x)|\le1\), \(|\tau(x)|=|\mu_1(x)-\mu_0(x)|\le2\), and subtraction of the two identified arm means identifies \(\tau(x)=\mathbb E[Y_1-Y_0\mid X=x]\), all for \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\).  Finally, the definitions of \(K_B\) and \(K_\Phi\), together with \(|A|\le1\) and \(|Y|\le1\), imply
\[
 |B_l(X)AY|\le K_B,
 \qquad \|F_{lj}(O)\|_2\le K_BK_\Phi,
 \qquad \|M_j(O)\|_2\le K_\Phi.
\]
These are bounds on every record in the operational privacy domain, not merely almost-sure bounds under one member of the model.
